items.headline: Singapore reclaims top spot in IMD World Competitiveness Ranking 2026
items.summary: Singapore returned to first place in IMD's 2026 World Competitiveness Ranking of 70 economies, pushing Hong Kong to second and Switzerland to third on the back of strong business-efficiency scores.

items.headline: NUS slips to 10th and NTU holds 12th in QS World University Rankings 2027
items.summary: In the QS World University Rankings 2027 released on June 18, NUS fell two places to 10th, the only Asian university in the global top 10, while NTU held 12th.

items.headline: Indonesia market rout sparks a cross-border Sell Singapore online feud
items.summary: A 'Sell Singapore' hashtag spread among Indonesian users after the rupiah slid past 18,000 per US dollar and Jakarta's stock index shed roughly a third of its value this year.

items.headline: Singapore Air Force Museum reopens after revamp with augmented-reality exhibits
items.summary: The RSAF's Air Force Museum near Paya Lebar reopened on June 17 after a months-long renovation, adding immersive exhibits; Zaqy Mohamad officiated.

items.headline: Update: Delhi High Court issues notice on Telegram's plea against India ban
items.summary: The Delhi High Court issued notice to the Centre on Telegram's challenge to the block in place until June 22 before the June 21 NEET-UG re-exam, granting no interim relief.

items.headline: Six women killed as a speeding tractor hits an e-rickshaw in UP's Badaun
items.summary: Six women returning from a wedding visit were killed when a tractor struck their e-rickshaw in Badaun, UP, on June 17; both drivers were detained.

items.headline: Rupee firms to 94.29 and Brent hits a three-month low as Hormuz reopens
items.summary: The rupee strengthened about 31 paise to 94.29 per US dollar on June 17 as Brent eased toward a three-month low near $79 with the Strait of Hormuz reopening.

items.headline: Modi to release 2,400 crore rupees in job incentives under PM-VBRY scheme
items.summary: PM Modi is set to disburse about 2,400 crore rupees in employment-linked incentives under the PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana in New Delhi on June 19.

items.headline: Update: Trump and Iran sign accord to end the war and reopen the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Trump and Iranian President Pezeshkian signed a 14-point memorandum ending their conflict, reopening the Strait of Hormuz toll-free and opening a 60-day window on Iran's uranium.

items.headline: Ukraine launches its largest drone assault on Moscow, hitting an oil refinery
items.summary: Ukraine struck Moscow with what Kyiv called its biggest drone assault of the war, hitting the Gazprom Neft refinery and injuring at least 17; Moscow airports suspended flights.

items.headline: Hegseth orders a six-month review of US forces in Europe and demands a NATO overhaul
items.summary: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth announced a six-month review of US troop posture in Europe and called for a 'NATO 3.0', urging allies to reach 5% of GDP on defence by 2035.

items.headline: Gaza death toll since the October ceasefire passes 1,000, officials say
items.summary: Gaza's health ministry said at least 1,005 Palestinians have been killed by Israeli fire since the ceasefire began on October 10, 2025.

items.headline: Vance warns Israel it cannot kill its way out of insecurity and is deeply isolated
items.summary: VP JD Vance told the New York Times that Israel is 'deeply isolated' and urged its leaders to back the Iran deal, singling out ministers Smotrich and Ben-Gvir.

items.headline: Amazon in talks to sell its Nvidia-rival AI chips to outside customers
items.summary: Amazon's Peter DeSantis said AWS is in early talks to sell its custom Trainium AI chips to other companies, a direct challenge to Nvidia.

items.headline: Transformer co-author Noam Shazeer leaves Google to join OpenAI
items.summary: Noam Shazeer, co-author of the 'Attention Is All You Need' paper and a Gemini co-lead, is joining OpenAI as lead for AI architecture research ahead of its IPO.

items.headline: Intel jumps about 10% after Trump says it will make chips with Apple
items.summary: Intel shares rose roughly 10% after Trump said Intel and Apple struck a deal to make semiconductors in the US, cutting Apple's reliance on TSMC.

items.headline: General Intuition in talks to raise $300 million at a $2 billion valuation
items.summary: General Intuition, which trains AI agents on game-clip data, is in talks to raise around $300 million at just over a $2 billion valuation, reportedly with Bezos and Schmidt backing.

items.headline: Pramaana Labs raises $27 million to bring formal verification to AI
items.summary: Pramaana Labs raised a $27 million seed led by Khosla Ventures to apply formal-verification methods to AI in high-stakes fields.

items.headline: EQT agrees to buy UK testing group Intertek for 60 pounds a share
items.summary: Swedish buyout firm EQT agreed to acquire Intertek for 60 pounds a share in cash, valuing it at roughly 11 billion pounds including debt; Intertek will leave the LSE.

items.headline: Accenture shares slump to worst day in years on a weak revenue outlook
items.summary: Accenture cut the top of its annual revenue-growth forecast to 3-4% from 3-5%, sending shares to their steepest drop in years, and unveiled $4.18 billion in cybersecurity deals.

items.headline: Norway's Norges Bank holds its rate at 4.25% and signals another hike
items.summary: Norges Bank kept its policy rate at 4.25% on June 18 and lifted its projected rate path to signal borrowing costs rising above 4.5% by year-end.

items.headline: SpaceX ends its first public week up about 37%, worth near $2.4 trillion
items.summary: SpaceX closed its first Nasdaq week about 37% above its IPO price, valuing it near $2.4 trillion despite a two-day pullback; the IPO priced at $135 to raise about $75 billion.

items.headline: Eala stuns world No. 2 Rybakina to reach the Berlin quarterfinals
items.summary: Wild card Alexandra Eala upset second seed Elena Rybakina 7-5, 6-4 in the Berlin round of 16 and next faces Elina Svitolina.

items.headline: Zverev reaches the Halle quarterfinals as a Shelton-Fritz clash is set
items.summary: Top seed Alexander Zverev beat Yannick Hanfmann 6-3, 7-6(4) to reach the Halle quarterfinals; Taylor Fritz and Ben Shelton set up an all-American last-eight tie.

items.headline: Keys beats Muchova to set a Berlin quarterfinal against Pegula
items.summary: Madison Keys beat Karolina Muchova in straight sets to reach the Berlin quarterfinals, where she meets Jessica Pegula.

items.headline: West Indies edge Scotland by seven runs at the Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: West Indies posted 153/6, with Stafanie Taylor unbeaten on 47 off 19, and held Scotland to 146 to win their Group 2 match at Headingley by seven runs.

items.headline: South Africa edge Pakistan by two wickets in a Women's T20 World Cup thriller
items.summary: South Africa scrambled to 127/8 to chase Pakistan's 126/9 with three overs to spare in Birmingham; Annerie Dercksen made 52 and was player of the match.

fun_fact.headline: A teaspoon of a neutron star would weigh about a billion tonnes
fun_fact.body: A neutron star squeezes up to twice the mass of our Sun into a sphere only about 20 kilometres across - roughly the size of a city. The matter is so dense that a single teaspoon of it would weigh about a billion tonnes on Earth.

puzzle.title: A Glass of Water
puzzle.body: A man asks a bartender for a glass of water; the bartender instead points a gun at him. The man says thank you and leaves without drinking. Why?
puzzle.approach: Ask why a request for water and a sudden scare could solve the same problem; think of a harmless bodily condition.
puzzle.answer: The man had the hiccups and wanted water to cure them. The bartender cured them faster by frightening him with the gun, so the man no longer needed the water and left grateful.
